bug: After an inline zero-duration Finish, the loop advances to the next future tick instead of dispatching the next queued customer at the same tick.
lesson: When an event completes synchronously, continue processing all newly enabled work at that same timestamp before advancing the simulation clock.

bug: When a customer finishes before the next arrival, the loop advances directly to that arrival without dispatching the waiting customer at the finish tick, so it starts late and computes the wrong wake surcharge.
lesson: When advancing a discrete-event simulation, process all state transitions at their actual event time before jumping to a later event.

bug: The parser validates numeric bases before confirming the entire base has valid syntax, so malformed items such as `999-x` can return OutOfRange instead of InvalidSyntax at the item start.
lesson: Validate an input’s complete structure before interpreting or range-checking any of its values.

bug: The parser validates the base numbers and range ordering before checking whether the step operand is syntactically valid, so malformed items can return numeric errors instead of InvalidSyntax at the item start.
lesson: Validate an entire construct’s required syntax before evaluating its values, while preserving the specified precedence between error classes.

bug: The parser validates a step number before validating the item’s base, so an invalid step can mask an earlier-required base syntax or numeric error.
lesson: Validate grammar and operands in the specified precedence order before evaluating dependent values.

bug: The parser validates step numbers before numeric bases and range endpoints, so a bad step can mask an earlier required base error.
lesson: Validate syntax first, then validate inputs in the order specified by the contract before processing dependent values.

bug: The parser validates step numbers before numeric bases and range endpoints, so a bad step can mask an earlier base error, contrary to the required error precedence.
lesson: Validate inputs in the specified order, and defer later-stage checks until all earlier-stage checks have succeeded.

bug: The parser accepts a numeric prefix followed by letters as an endpoint, then `parse_number` subtracts `b'0'` from the letter and can panic instead of returning `InvalidSyntax`.
lesson: Validate an entire token against its grammar before performing byte arithmetic or numeric conversion.

bug: parse_with drops a record that ends with a delimiter because it only emits the final record when field_started is true, losing the trailing empty field.
lesson: Track whether a record has begun independently of its current field contents so trailing delimiters preserve empty fields.

bug: In a quoted field, the parser treats any quote followed by another quote as an escape, so a closing quote immediately followed by an escaped quote is misread and can cause a valid field to be reported as unclosed.
lesson: Resolve ambiguous delimiters using the full grammar and remaining input context before committing to a token interpretation.

bug: The parser treats any quote at the start of a field as an opener, so after consuming an escaped quote pair at EOF it can incorrectly accept the field as closed instead of returning UnclosedQuote at the opening quote.
lesson: Track escape and closing states explicitly; distinguish a doubled escape from a closing delimiter even when input ends immediately afterward.

bug: The code checks for an unclosed quoted prefix after scanning separators, so MissingAt or separator errors can incorrectly take precedence over UnclosedQuote.
lesson: Enforce required validation precedence explicitly; perform each stage before any later-stage checks.

bug: For an empty interior component, validation reports the component’s starting slash (`i.saturating_sub(1)`) instead of its terminating slash, so `/a//b` returns 2 rather than 3.
lesson: Translate parser errors to the specified source offset explicitly; distinguish empty components’ delimiters from nonempty components’ starting bytes.

bug: Case detection uses any ASCII uppercase byte, so lowercase-only valid symbols such as `iv` are incorrectly classified as mixed case.
lesson: Derive classification from the first item that meets the specified criterion, then validate later items against it.

bug: A lone minus sign returns InvalidByte at the end, but the grammar requires a digit there and specifies the missing-digit offset as text.len(); this is the same offset here, so the actual defect is elsewhere: magnitude accumulation can overflow u128 on arbitrarily long digit sequences before returning OutOfRange.
lesson: When parsing unbounded numeric text, detect range overflow during digit accumulation instead of accumulating into a fixed-width integer.

bug: parse_magnitude accumulates arbitrarily long digit tokens in u128, so debug builds can panic on overflow before returning the required OutOfRange parse error.
lesson: When parsing unbounded numeric input, detect limit overflow during digit-by-digit conversion instead of accumulating in a fixed-width type.

bug: parse_magnitude can overflow u128 while processing an arbitrarily long digit sequence, causing a debug panic instead of the required OutOfRange parse error.
lesson: When parsing unbounded numeric input, detect range overflow incrementally and return the specified error instead of accumulating into a fixed-width integer.

bug: When a leading minus is not followed by a digit, parse reports the position after the minus instead of the first invalid byte at offset 0.
lesson: Track the grammar state that failed and report the earliest byte that violates the complete input grammar.

bug: parse_magnitude can overflow u128 on arbitrarily long digit sequences, so it may panic in debug builds or wrap and misclassify the required OutOfRange error.
lesson: When parsing unbounded numeric input, detect range overflow during digit accumulation instead of relying on a wider integer type.

bug: The particular solution is allocated before checking whether the system is Unique, so an overflowing n*k shape incorrectly returns ShapeOverflow even when the required result is Infinite and only n*f must be representable.
lesson: Check each output shape for overflow immediately before constructing that output, and avoid validating shapes that the selected result does not require.

bug: The parser returns InvalidByte as soon as it sees a missing numerator or denominator digit, so inputs like "/1" or "1/" can skip full grammar validation and the required syntax-error precedence.
lesson: Validate the entire input grammar and record its first violation before applying semantic checks.

bug: The iterative DFS can push multiple pending copies of a vertex, so a dense graph can exhaust the call stack’s memory and panic despite being within the input limits.
lesson: Bound auxiliary memory explicitly when traversing dense graphs; avoid storing redundant pending work items.

bug: When a word suffix does not fit, usable marker selection checks prefix-plus-hyphen against the remaining room but fails to reserve the separating space on a nonempty line, so it can append a fragment that exceeds the line width.
lesson: Account for every required separator and decoration when checking whether content fits within a bounded capacity.

bug: The optimizer stores only one best candidate per word index, so it cannot represent distinct continuation states at scalar offsets inside a word and may miss the globally optimal layout and tie-break vector.
lesson: When a specification defines multiple state dimensions, include every dimension in the optimization state and memoization key.

bug: For bracketed IPv6 hosts, the parser accepts the first closing bracket without rejecting an additional `]` in the suffix, so malformed literals can pass as valid URLs.
lesson: Validate the complete token against its grammar, including trailing delimiters, rather than accepting a valid prefix.

bug: An IPv6 literal followed by `:` and an empty port reports InvalidPort at the position after the colon, but the required empty-port offset is immediately after that colon; this implementation calculates the offset one byte too far.
lesson: Derive error offsets from the original input’s delimiter positions, and verify boundary cases for every parsing branch.

bug: For relative paths, the resolver parses the constructed URL before normalizing the merged path, so component-validation errors can precede path-normalization errors despite the required normalization sequence.
lesson: When a specification defines validation stages and their error precedence, preserve that order explicitly across intermediate transformations.

bug: The resolver rebuilds an inherited URL from parsed fields, losing the original spelling of an explicit port by serializing its numeric value (for example, `:80` is preserved but its raw representation cannot be preserved when formatting differs).
lesson: Preserve source text for values whose spelling must survive parsing and reconstruction; semantic conversion alone may discard required representation.

bug: decode_many calls Vec::with_capacity(count) before decoding, so a huge count can panic or abort on capacity overflow despite the no-panic requirement.
lesson: Avoid allocating from untrusted size parameters before establishing a safe bound or using a fallible allocation strategy.

bug: decode_u64 checks for a missing byte before checking whether it is byte ten, so a ten-byte prefix with continuation set returns Truncated instead of Overflow.
lesson: Apply boundary-specific error precedence before general missing-input checks.

bug: StreamDecoder::push increments the absolute position with unchecked addition, which can overflow and panic when committed input reaches usize::MAX.
lesson: Use checked arithmetic for counters that can grow with untrusted input, and handle overflow without panicking.

bug: StreamDecoder::push increments position with unchecked addition, so a committed length near usize::MAX can overflow and panic or wrap.
lesson: Use checked arithmetic for counters that represent accumulated input, and define behavior at the type’s numeric limit.
